title: Once you've fixed the bug that sent messages to the Dead Letter Queue, how do you reprocess them: the "redrive" flow of moving messages from the DLQ back to the main topic/queue so consumers retry them: and how do you do it safely (inspect/replay/discard tooling, idempotent consumers so replays don't cause duplicate side-effects, avoiding re-poisoning the main topic)?
shortTitle: Reprocessing dead letter queue messages safely (the redrive flow)
keyPoints: Redrive moves DLT records back to the main flow under operator control after the root-cause bug is fixed.
The precondition is a deployed fix -- replaying before fixing just re-fills the DLT.
Inspection: read DLT records and error metadata to classify which records to replay, correct, or discard.
Selective replay: republish to a reprocessing topic (not the live main topic) with the original key preserved.
Idempotent consumers are essential so replayed records do not cause duplicate side effects like double debits.
Throttle replay rate to avoid overwhelming consumers or downstream dependencies.
Never blindly loop the entire DLT back -- still-poisonous records re-poison the main topic.

s1_definition.oneliner: Redrive moves dead letter records back to the main flow under operator control, and it is safe only when consumers are idempotent and you inspect, selectively replay, or discard rather than blindly pushing everything back.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Redrive** -- the controlled process of moving records from a dead letter queue back into the main topic or a reprocessing topic so that fixed consumers can handle them.
- **Inspection** -- reading DLT records and their error metadata to classify which records should be replayed, corrected, or discarded.
- **Selective replay** -- republishing only the records that should be reprocessed, preserving the original key, usually to a dedicated reprocessing topic.
- **Idempotent consumers** -- consumers that produce the same result whether they see a record once or many times, keyed on a business id.
- **Reprocessing topic** -- a dedicated topic for replayed records, isolating replay traffic from live traffic and allowing throttling.
- **Re-poisoning** -- the anti-pattern of blindly looping DLT records back to the main topic, causing still-poisonous records to fail again.
s1_definition.analogy: The dead letter queue is National Bank of India's problem tray full of transfer forms that failed. Once the bug is fixed, redrive is the supervisor carefully taking forms out of the problem tray and putting them back in the normal processing line. The supervisor first reads each form to confirm it is now processable (inspect), only puts back the good ones (replay), bins the junk ones (discard), and the clerks downstream recognize I already processed this exact form so nobody is charged twice (idempotent consumers). The supervisor never dumps the whole tray back blindly.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Redrive Flow

  ┌──────────────────┐
  │ transfers.DLT    │
  │ (dead letter)    │
  └───────┬──────────┘
          │
          ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │ INSPECT          │
  │ Read records +   │
  │ error metadata   │
  └───────┬──────────┘
          │
    ┌─────┴─────┐
    │           │
    ▼           ▼
  REPLAY     DISCARD
  (fixable)  (garbage)
    │           │
    ▼           ▼
  ┌────────┐  Audit
  │ reprocess │  trail
  │ topic     │
  └────┬──────┘
       │ (throttled)
       ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │ Settlement       │
  │ Consumer         │
  │ (idempotent)     │
  │ TXN-001: skip    │
  │ TXN-002: settle  │
  └──────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Redrive is the controlled process of moving records from the dead letter queue back into the main flow after the root-cause bug is fixed. The absolute precondition is that the fix is deployed, because replaying before fixing just re-fills the DLT.

A safe redrive has three capabilities: inspection to classify each record and its error, selective replay to a dedicated reprocessing topic with the original key preserved and throttled rate, and discard with an audit trail for genuinely unprocessable records. The safety pillar is idempotent consumers, so a replayed record that was partially processed before failing is recognized and skipped rather than double-applied.

At National Bank of India, a bug once falsely rejected large transfers and sent them to transfers.DLT. After Rajesh fixed and deployed the correction, the team ran an audited, rate-limited redrive that inspected each record, replayed the processable ones to a reprocessing topic, and discarded the malformed ones. Because the settlement consumer is idempotent on the trade id, a partially-applied transfer was recognized on replay and skipped.

Remember one sentence: redrive is an explicit, observable, reversible operator action built on idempotent consumers and careful classification, not an automatic retry loop.
